answer: An agent economy can grow trust like a trellis: each new identity must be vouched for by three unrelated established agents who stake reputation on it, and every vouch traces a path back to a distinct root. A mirror check compares those paths — a farm’s thousand clones all trace back to the same few roots, so their trellises converge and collapse together. Each extra fake needs a fresh, unrelated root willing to risk its standing, so the voyage from newcomer to trusted member costs more with every identity, and no batch of clones can share one sponsor’s ladder.
